finding.summary: Gesture workqueue creation failure was unchecked, gesture callbacks scheduled through the possibly null queue, and teardown destroyed the queue without closing new submissions.
evidence: ufp_mac_init stores alloc_workqueue() directly and continues initialization without checking for NULL.
The recovered gesture callback unconditionally calls mod_delayed_work_on() with the stored queue.
The recovered exit body unconditionally flushes and destroys the stored queue, and it has no admission gate against concurrent gesture reporting.

change.mechanism: A mutex serializes publication of the platform device, gesture event forwarding/scheduling, and workqueue shutdown.
change.allocation_failure: Gesture uevents continue when the platform device exists; delayed work is skipped if the queue allocation failed.
teardown_order: mark lifecycle stopping and clear the queue slot while holding the mutex
flush and destroy the queue only if non-NULL
clear the platform-device pointer under the mutex
change.race_property: A reporter that enters first completes its queue submission before teardown closes admission; reporters entering after the stop gate do not access the device or queue.

limits: Canonical build and byte reproducibility passed; runtime event behavior and NX809J hardware teardown were not exercised.
The queue-allocation failure path is handled by skipping delayed scheduling while preserving the uevent.
